summary: Both gas pages rebuilt and verified. (A) gas-delivery-charge-vs-supply-charge.md: corrected the Columbia Gas of Ohio miscategorization — the '$3.25 added to NYMEX' example is Ohio's Standard Choice Offer, a SUPPLY mechanism, now re-categorized with the utility's live SCO calculation; added a full dated sources layer (7 sources, all fetched 2026-08-29); ConEd's tax claim re-verified at current wording ('nearly a quarter of the delivery charge', plus new $3.2B 2026 figure); removed Localsyr electricity stat and replaced with ConEd's gas-domain winter-demand mechanism + EIA seasonality; dropped National Grid 'semiannual GAF' (unverifiable on current page); kept and upgraded the comparison table and worked example. (B) 12-how-to-read-your-gas-bill.md: removed the unsupported '80–150 therms' RECS monthly band and installed the climate-zone framing ('100–200 therms peak winter, 10–40 summer') anchored to EIA monthly consumption shares (Jan ≈19% of annual, Jul ≈2.4%, 2020–2024) and RECS 2020 CE5.4 annual data (~860 therms/yr cold-climate gas-heated homes, heating ≈73%); removed dead DOE PDF citation; re-verified all prices, added NIPSCO/National Grid/Columbia verification examples; added a 'Reconciling Related Guides' section aligning 07's ~200-therm winter example and mcf-vs-ccf-vs-therms' 100–150 CCF band (≈104–156 therms) with the one consistent band now used across my files.
findings: COLUMBIA MISCATEGORIZATION CONFIRMED AND FIXED: columbiagasohio.com's SCO page (retrieved 2026-08-29) shows the Standard Choice Offer is the default SUPPLY price: NYMEX month-end settlement ($2.7250/Mcf, Aug 2026) + Retail Price Adjustment ($2.25/Mcf, Jan 2026 PUCO auction) = $4.975/Mcf = $0.4975/Ccf. The old '$3.25 per Mcf' no longer appears on the page (unverifiable → dropped). File A now carries a visible correction note so the prior error is documented, not silently buried.

ConEd CURRENT wording differs from the remembered anchor: the page now says embedded local taxes 'make up nearly a quarter of the delivery charge you pay' (not 'about one quarter') and adds a fresh citable figure: 'In 2026, we expect our customers will pay more than $3.2 billion in local taxes on energy infrastructure.' File A quotes the current wording.

NIPSCO's live gas-bill page verifies the fixed-fee structure but with different wording than the article had: delivery 'includes a basic customer fee' and both supply and 'parts of the Delivery Charge' are usage-based — quoted exactly rather than paraphrased.

National Grid verifies supply-vs-delivery split ('National Grid is a delivery company... we will deliver gas to you regardless of your choice of supplier'; 'you pay what we pay'; GAF = Gas Supply Charge) but NO 'semiannual/Nov-May' wording exists on the current page → the old semiannual claim was dropped, not kept.

Wave-2's RECS limitation confirmed first-hand: RECS 2020 CE tables are annual-only; no monthly usage data exists in RECS. The replacement band is therefore anchored to EIA's monthly national consumption series (Jan ≈19.0%, Jul ≈2.4% of annual residential gas use, 2020–2024 avg; Jan:Jul ≈ 7.9:1) plus RECS CE5.4 cold-climate annual total (607 Ccf heating + 184 water + 41 cooking/dryer ≈ 860 therms/yr; heating ≈73%). A simple seasonal model using these fetched numbers yields Jan ≈139 / Jul ≈35 therms — independently landing inside the mission's suggested 100–200 / 10–40 band.

DOE PDF (energy.gov/sites/default/files/2021-11/Understanding+Your+Natural+Gas+Bills.pdf) confirmed HTTP 404 → citation removed from 12 per site standards. All replacement sources verified live 2026-08-29.

EIA prices re-verified live: 2024 $14.50/Mcf, 2025 $15.34/Mcf national residential; CA $22.01, FL $25.48, HI $52.38, CO $11.17, ID $7.69, MI $10.92, NY $17.58 (2025 state summary). The NY $17.58 figure was added to File B's price paragraph.

Conversion ground re-verified at EIA Btu page: 1 cf = 1,036 Btu, 1 therm = 100,000 Btu → 1 Ccf ≈ 103,600 Btu ≈ 1.03–1.04 therms; File B's worked example now uses the article's own stated 1.037 factor consistently (60 Ccf × 1.037 = 62.2 therms; 62.2 × $1.40 = $87.08, both recomputed by command).

One consistent band installed across MY two files: File B states '100–200 therms deep-winter peak / 10–40 summer' and explicitly reconciles 07 (≈200-therm winter example = upper part of the range) and mcf-vs-ccf-vs-therms (100–150 CCF ≈ 104–156 therms). File A deliberately states no thermostat numbers, so no internal conflict exists.

Unverifiable-on-current-pages content removed rather than kept: $3.25/Mcf, 'semiannual' GAF review, Localsyr electricity-generation quote, the old 'fixed fees $7–$15' range, '$0.10–$0.50/therm typical', the prior table's unverifiable 2020-2021-era price rows, and '5–10× higher january bill' (replaced with the measured ≈8:1 volume ratio, cited).
